impl.summary: N7-11 built on top of N7-1/N7-2's layout library and plan (nothing duplicated). Storyboard gets a 'One sheet' option: the whole board is drawn as one MOSS-Image page (multi_panel layout, one object box per panel with its shot), on oss-moss-image (your GPU) or moss-image (fal). The browser shows each panel from the sheet and cuts it out (canvas crop, then upload) when you Animate or Edit it. Following the brief's 'gate behind a GPU test result', the option is shown only to the owner, marked as not yet tested on a GPU, until a result is recorded in ONE_SHEET_GPU_TEST; after that everyone gets it, up to the panel count that result records. Layers gets a new 'Re-render from layers' tool. Each visible layer's rotation-aware bounds, clipped to the canvas, plus its name or prompt become an object or character item. Layers that fill the canvas are named in the caption as the backdrop. OCR lines from the latest whole-picture text detection become text items with their exact words. The job runs this as text-to-image with the layout on the picture's nearest aspect ratio, and the result lands as a new layer on top with the original layers kept underneath. Models: open oss-moss-image; cloud moss-image (default), ideogram-4-5 and flux-3. The existing planLayout compiles the layout per model and turns prompt expansion and the enhancer off. The colour / depth control part was not built: it needs the ComfyUI pin bump.

That needs a new graph (scripts/comfy entry plus model-pins.json pin) and a GPU test. There is no hosted equivalent, so the cloud keeps the box layout.

Both features use existing routes (POST /api/storyboards, /api/storyboards/estimate, /api/layers/:id/jobs), which already follow the guest/account rules.

findings.title: Re-render: the backdrop is dropped from the prompt whenever the person types a description
findings.detail: layersLayout(doc, text, words) builds the caption as '<words>. Behind everything: <backdrop>.' when words are given, and the tool shows '· N backdrop layer described in words'. But RerenderTool sends prompt: words.trim(), and jobSteps uses `prompt || layout.summary.caption`. planLayout then replaces the draft caption with that prompt. So the 'Behind everything: …' part never reaches the model. Verified with a scratch probe: a full-canvas layer named 'a beach at dusk' plus words 'warm photo' gives the draft caption 'warm photo. Behind everything: a beach at dusk.', but the planned moss-image prompt contains no 'beach'. Fix: let the layout's caption win for rerender (send no separate prompt, or have jobSteps use layout.summary.caption when the layout carries one), and add a test that a backdrop survives typed words.

findings.title: A second re-render treats the first result as the backdrop named 'Re-render'
findings.detail: apply.ts lands the result as a visible, opaque, full-canvas node named 'Re-render', and its prompt goes on the revision, not on node.prompt. On the next run layersLayout counts it as a backdrop (area >= 0.9). 'Re-render' is not in GENERIC_NAME, so the caption says 'Behind everything: Re-render.' and the status line counts an extra backdrop layer. That layer also hides every layer the run boxes. Either skip earlier re-render layers (or every hidden-by-cover result) or add 're-render' to GENERIC_NAME.

findings.title: A sliver of a layer left on the canvas fails the whole re-render with 'Box 1 has no size: draw it again'
findings.detail: intersect() keeps any positive overlap, but frac() rounds to 1e-6, so a layer whose on-canvas part is thinner than about 1e-6 of the canvas produces a zero-width box. validateLayout then refuses the run with a message that makes no sense in Layers. Verified with a probe: a 4000 px canvas with a layer at x=3999.9999 gives box [1,0,1,0.0125] and 'Box 1 has no size: draw it again'. This is rare, but the fix is cheap: drop boxes under about 1 px in layersLayout.

findings.title: A failed or cancelled sheet's header says 'on the way'
findings.detail: The header reads `${done ? 'done' : 'on the way'}`, and done counts only succeeded generations. A failed or cancelled sheet therefore shows 'N panels on one sheet · on the way' next to the FailedTile. It should say failed when first.status is failed or canceled. Retrying, as the implementer noted, re-posts through /api/generations, whose schema drops request.frame, so the retried sheet shows as a plain frame.

findings.title: The One sheet gate and the panel cap are enforced only in the browser
findings.detail: sheetPanelLimit / ONE_SHEET_GPU_TEST only hide the pill and cap the counter in the UI. POST /api/storyboards and /estimate accept sheet:true with up to MAX_FRAMES panels from any caller allowed to reach them. Today this is harmless, because POST /api/storyboards is a library change and so owner-only (tests/public-signup.test.ts storyboards family). Once a GPU result is recorded, though, the recorded maxPanels is not enforced server-side. planOneSheet could clamp to sheetPanelLimit(true) instead. Also, after a test with maxPanels < 8, manual mode silently drops scenes past the limit that were written before One sheet was picked (filled.slice(0, sheetLimit)) without saying so.

review.verdict: approve with fixes: the build matches the brief (One sheet on oss-moss-image / moss-image, gated to the owner until a GPU result is recorded; Re-render from layers on MOSS on both engines plus Ideogram 4.5 / FLUX.3 in the cloud; the colour / depth control is correctly left out and what it needs is recorded). applied: MEDIUM (src/server/layers.ts): when the person typed words, Re-render dropped the backdrop from the prompt. The cause was that jobSteps used `prompt || layout.summary.caption`. The new rerenderCaption(caption, prompt) makes the layout's caption win: the browser builds that caption from the typed words plus 'Behind everything: <backdrop>'. If words come in beside a caption that doesn't already start with them (an API caller), they are put in front of it, so neither the words nor the backdrop is lost. Test: a full-canvas 'a beach at dusk' layer plus the words 'warm photo' gives the request prompt 'warm photo. Behind everything: a beach at dusk.' on oss-moss-image, moss-image, ideogram-4-5 and flux-3, and the planned prompt contains 'a beach at dusk'. Also covers rerenderCaption's edge cases. The existing assertion for a typed prompt beside an auto caption was updated to match.

LOW (src/lib/layers.ts): a second re-render counted the first result as a backdrop named 'Re-render'. layersLayout now skips any node whose active revision label is TOOL_LABELS.rerender. 're-render' is added to GENERIC_NAME, so a renamed or copied one reads as 'a picture element'. RerenderTool now sends TOOL_LABELS.rerender as the job label instead of a literal string. Test added.

LOW (src/lib/layers.ts): a sliver of a layer on the canvas failed the whole run with 'Box 1 has no size'. layersLayout now keeps a layer or text box only when its part on the canvas is at least 1 px each way. Test: a layer at x=399.9999 on a 400 px canvas and a text box 0.5 px wide are both dropped, and the job plans without an error.

LOW (src/components/storyboard-view.tsx, src/lib/catalog/storyboard.ts): a failed or cancelled sheet's header said 'on the way'. The new sheetState(status) returns done, failed, cancelled or on the way, and the header uses it. Test added.

LOW (src/lib/catalog/storyboard.ts): the panel cap was enforced only in the browser. planOneSheet(input, test = ONE_SHEET_GPU_TEST) now refuses more panels than sheetPanelLimit(true, test), with 'A one-sheet board has at most N panels…', and refuses everything when the recorded test allows 0. Today nothing changes, because no test is recorded and the owner gets MAX_FRAMES. Test added with a recorded 6-panel result.
